brief.subject: Court sides with NY on CDLs; AI cargo theft tops $150M
brief.headline: Appeals Court Overturns NY Funding Denial Over Non-Domiciled CDLs
brief.dek: New York wins a CDL funding fight, AI cargo theft passes $150 million, Mexico tariffs threatened, and LA rail dwell tops nine days.
brief.lede: A federal appeals court unanimously overturned DOT's denial of funds to New York in a dispute over how long non-domiciled CDLs stay valid.

sections.heading: NY Wins Non-Domiciled CDL Fight
bullets: Unanimous: a three-judge Second Circuit panel sided with New York against the Department of Transportation.
The fight centered on how long a non-domiciled CDL can remain in effect, plus DOT withholding funds from the state.
Watch for ripple effects on driver licensing rules and on how other states issue these CDLs.

sections.heading: Fake Carriers Drive Cargo Theft
bullets: More than $150 million in AI equipment was stolen from June 2025 to June 2026, per Overhaul.
92% of reported incidents involved fraudulent carrier identities and falsified shipping documents, putting legitimate carriers' identities at risk.
A suspect in the $100 million Brink's jewelry theft agreed to plead guilty in a related cargo robbery case.
Court records show the group tracked commercial trucks and hit unattended loads, a reminder to limit unattended stops on high-value freight.

sections.heading: Tariff Threats on Mexico Freight
bullets: The president threatened to double tariffs on Mexico immediately unless it halts migrant caravans into the U.S.
Cross-border carriers could see sudden volume swings if the higher levies take effect.
Three bills in Congress would significantly restrict presidential tariff power if they become law.

sections.heading: LA Rail Dwell Tops Nine Days
bullets: Over nine days: rail-bound containers are sitting idle at the Port of Los Angeles, per Executive Director Gene Seroka.
Slow rail can push more Southern California freight onto trucks and stretch drayage wait times.

sections.heading: USPS Raises Rates, Adds Surcharge
bullets: 5.9% average price increase planned in January for services like USPS Ground Advantage and Priority Mail.
11% permanent fuel surcharge is coming alongside the parcel rate hike.
Higher postal costs may nudge some shippers toward other parcel and final-mile options.
